entry.dc:title: Geophysical reconnaissance to assess a site affected by shallow opencast mining
entry.dc:creator: Booth A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Bulletin of the International Association of Engineering Geology Bulletin De L Association Internationale De Geologie De L Ingenieur
entry.dc:description: La condition physique du sol d'un chantier de construction a été étudiée. Le terrain avait été exploité par endroits et les trous de faible profondeur qui en résultaient avaient été comblés de remblai. Pour fixer l'emplacement des maisons, et pour faciliter l'étude de leurs fondations, il fallait d'abord faire un plan de ces trous remblayés. On traça, à partir des résultats des essais séismiques et des contrôles d'impédance électrique du sol, des courbes d'égale vitesse de propagation des ondes et d'égale résistivité électrique, et on compara avec l'expérience et avec le témoignage des archives d'activité minière. Il est en général possible de localiser, à partir des résultats de cette étude, les zones qui sont composées de matériaux peu compactés. On put répérer les régions qui pouvaient poser des problèmes pour la construction, ce qui permit de faire une étude efficace et plus économique. Les maisons sont actuellement en cours de réalisation.

entry.dc:title: Asset stripping (UK).
entry.dc:description: As open cast mining has expanded in scale in recent years, public opposition has become more vocal. One notable consequence has been the setting up of the Opencast Mining Intelligence Group and their report 'A reassessment of opencast coalmining' is discussed by the author. -from Author

entry.dc:title: What will be the price for energy tomorrow?. I. Coal price.
entry.dc:creator: Ippolito M.
entry.dc:description: Traces the evolution of the coal industry in the developed world and looks to opencast mining in the southern continents as the sources of cheap supplies in the future, even when transport costs are taken into full consideration.-H.Clout

entry.dc:title: Sedimentary structures in Quaternary ironsands at Waikato North Head, New Zealand
entry.dc:creator: Christie A.B.
entry.prism:publicationName: New Zealand Journal of Geology and Geophysics
entry.dc:description: Opencast mining at Waikato North Head, Franklin County, South Auckland, New Zealand, has exposed the sedimentary structures in Late Quaternary titanomagnetite ironsands of two units of the Kaihu Group: the Waiuku Blacksand Member (Hood Formation) and the Entrican Dune Member (Mitiwai Formation). The Waiuku Blacksand Member consists of a series of alternating, steeply cross-laminated and horizontally laminated sand units, which are sometimes separated by units of mud. The very large scale of the cross-laminated sets (up to 12 m thick), their orientation, grain size and internal features suggest an eolian origin. Some of the horizontally laminated units are topset beds associated with the foresets of the cross-laminated units, whereas others are of either interdune stream-lake, or beach origin. Mud units may represent soils, loess, or interdune swamp and lake deposits. The Entrican Dune Member consists of large migrating dunes which were stabilised in this area by afforestation in 1935. Internally, they are composed of large and very large sets of steeply inclined, cross-lamination (foresets) and large sets of horizontal lamination, or low angle crosslamination (topsets). © 1979 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.

entry.dc:title: Brown coal opencast mining and landscaping in the rhineland
entry.dc:creator: Kausch P.
entry.dc:description: The brown coal deposits in the world form an important reserve of energy and raw material, which can also be widely used economically in the present state of opencast mining techniques. Rhenish brown coal mining with its high values of production and productivity proves also that brown coal deposits, though low in energy, are economically exploitable if, for the mining of this coal, necessary preconditions are fulfilled. These are large‐scale mining fields and the use of an appropriate opencast mining technique which includes reclamation and landscaping after mining. the measures necessary for this and the technical development have been carried out by mining Rhenish brown coal on an economical basis. Thanks to the rich deposit reserves, to the high level of development of the opencast mining technique as well as to new or further development of refining processes, Rhenish brown coal mining will also be able in the future, to contribute considerably to securing the supply of energy and raw material. Copyright © 1979 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.
entry.authkeywords: Brown coal | Land reclamation | Opencast mining

entry.dc:title: Investigation on the methods of forecasting changes in the physicogeographical environment on the basis of the Konin area.
entry.dc:creator: Kozacki L.
entry.dc:description: Discusses the prediction of changes that will result from a major opencast mining development in Tertiary and Quaternary sediments. Changes in relief, groundwater levels and the pattern of revegetation are covered.-K.Clayton

entry.dc:title: Analysis Results for Building an Opencast Mine for the Exploitation of the ″Djurakov Do″ Bauxite Deposit.
entry.dc:creator: Jujic D.
entry.dc:description: Both opencast and underground methods were considered for mining Yugoslavia's Djurakov Do bauxite deposit, and it was concluded that opencast mining would be more attractive from economical and other standpoints. The deposit was divided into five blocks, each with differant mining characteristics, in order to facilitate the evaluation. Several opencast design variations were developed for the selection of an optimum design with specific parameters.

entry.dc:title: OPENCAST MINING MACHINERY FROM EAST GERMANY.
entry.dc:creator: Sealy T.
entry.dc:description: An earlier article dealt with the important brown coal mining industry in the German Democratic Republic (DDR) and outlined the current operations and future plans for the industry. In this follow-up article, the type of machinery manufactured in East Germany for strip mining operations is considered and examples are given of th use of such machinery outside the DDR. The machinery covered includes conveyors and bucket ladder excavators.

entry.dc:title: The archaeology of the Coal Measures and the Magnesian Limestone escarpment in Co. Durham: a preliminary survey.
entry.dc:creator: Turnbull P.
entry.dc:description: The first systematic study of the poorly understood lowland areas of the county used information from tithe maps, OS records, and vertical air photographs, with some follow-up field walking. Many new sites were revealed; buildings and industrial monuments are also listed. Recommendations are made for meeting the threats from opencast mining and stone quarrying and appendices treat the vegetational history, the place-names, and comparative landscape histories of three individual parishes.-from British Archaeological Abstracts

entry.dc:title: Determining topographic surface on contour plans in recultivation.
entry.dc:creator: Dimov L.
entry.dc:description: Discusses the rational shaping of the surface of embankments and fills on land affected by opencast mining. Possible approaches to the problem of planning suitable surfaces are given: analytical, graphic-analytical and graphic. A detailed examination is made of the graphic method of vertical planning with the aid of projected contours on 1:2000 and 1:5000 topographic plans. -from Abstracts of Bulgarian Scientific Literature

entry.dc:title: Limits of environmental protection considered from the viewpoint of the opencast mining and quarrying industry
entry.dc:creator: Goeke H.
entry.dc:description: Based on the conceptions of environment and environmental protection, the author takes a look at the need for protective measures. The limits of environmental protection are equated to the limits of what the world of human industrial activity can be expected to tolerate, and a note of warning is sounded against one-sided loading of the demands imposed. The importance of the pit and quarry industry is outlined. Various environmental problems associated with interventions in the landscape and with pollutant emissions are discussed, and licensing procedures are explained.

entry.dc:title: Groundwater control in opencast mining of a lignite deposit in southern Greece.
entry.dc:creator: Spiliotis G.
entry.prism:publicationName: In Proc Siamos 78 Int Symp on Water in Mining and Underground Works Granada Spain Sep 18 22 1978 Granada Spai
entry.dc:description: This paper describes the method adopted for the protection of the northern part of the Megalopolis lignite mine, against hazards resulting from inundation due to groundwater inflow. The groundwater is confined in a karstic aquifer below the floor of the opencast mine and the respective hydrogeological conditions are described. Also included are descriptions of field examination by pumping tests, and the interpretation of the test results. Finally, the paper deals with the design of a pumping system for the protection of the mine, and the economical data concerning the installation and the operation of this sytem. (A)

entry.dc:title: BUTTERWELL.
entry.dc:creator: Batchelor M.
entry.dc:description: Contract opencast mining accounts for an important part of U. K. coal output. This article deals with a new opencast operation at Butterwell in north-east England, which provides a good example of such a contract, being a multi-seam mine using modern excavation and haulage equipment. The contract for mining at Butterwell involves the productionof 12 million tonnes of coal over 10 years. The geology of the coal seams, initial operations at the mine, as well as future plans are outlined.

entry.dc:title: OPENCAST COAL MINING IN THE UNITED KINGDOM AND ITS ROLE IN THE MINING INDUSTRY.
entry.dc:creator: Davidson D.
entry.dc:description: The author examines the trends in opencast coal mining in the U. K. and shows how the whole concept of opencast mining in that country has radically changed over the past 30 years. The future availability of opencast reserves in Great Britain is also discussed in terms of both technically workable and economically workable deposits. Finally, a brief description of the production techniques employed in opencast mining is given.

entry.dc:title: Opencast Mining of Coal in the Blanzy Basin of the Houilleres du Centre et du Midi.
entry.dc:creator: Cochon R.
entry.dc:description: The Blanzy basin, part of the Houilleres du Centre et du Midi, is the biggest opencast mining site in France, producing 700,000 tonnes of coal per year. This article examines in detail the equipment used at the mine: motorscrapers used for overburden removal, hydraulic shovels, tire loaders, dump tracks, and then deals briefly with auxiliary operations, environmental problems, and costs.

entry.dc:title: Opencast Mining of Coal in France.
entry.dc:creator: Iooss R.
entry.dc:description: The opencast mining method consists in removing the overburden situated above a coal deposit in order to exploit this deposit by the open-pit mining method. The author briefly examines the history of open cast mining of coal in France, and then describes the French coal deposits workable by this method. Proved reserves of these deposits, total 12 million tons, whereas possible reserves are estimated at 8 million tons. Technical details are given on the open cast mining method with particular reference to the type of machinery used, transport, land reclamation and minig costs.

entry.dc:title: FLUX GRADE LIMESTONE DEPOSITS OF JAGGAYYAPETA AREA, KRISHNA DISTRICT, ANDHRA PRADESH.
entry.dc:creator: Natarajan V.
entry.dc:description: A total of 134 million tonnes of flux-grade limestones, including 47 million tons of easily workable limestone, are estimated to exist in the area under study. The deposits lend themselves to easy, economical and largely mechanized opencast mining. The proven reserves alone could meet the needs of proposed steel plants in the southern part of India, since these limestones possess the necessary chemical and physical characteristics for use in blast furnaces. The geology of the area is also covered.

entry.dc:title: SCHEME OF DEVELOPING SEAMS BELOW WATER-LOGGED WORKINGS.
entry.dc:creator: Gulati A.K.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: Several disasters have occured in the past in Indian coal mines in which the old water-logged workings existed that had been exploited by opencast mining and inclines up to shallow depths. Therefore, an efficient system for proving the width of safety pillars in the old workings and of dewatering these has become a must. One of such systems, based on advance boring and adopted by the Sudamdih Incline Mine, is examined in detail here.

entry.dc:title: PRODUCING COAL.
entry.dc:creator: Rawlinson R.
entry.dc:description: In the U. K. 's Plan for Coal, it is envisaged that of the 150 million tons potential demand for coal in 1985, opencast mining would produce 15 million tons, the remaining 135 million tons to be obtained by deep mined output. If, as at present, 6. 75 million tons continue to be mined by shortwall and other similar systems, then the remaining 128. 25 million tons will have to be obtained from longwall mechanized faces. The author examines the areas for improvement of coal face equipment, and reviews some recent development in power loader design and practice, armored face conveyors, powered supports, and automatic steering of power leaders. The Advanced Technology Mining (ATM) concept is also considered.

entry.dc:title: Lignite Mining in the Rhine Basin.
entry.dc:creator: Penning H.
entry.dc:description: With lignite production totaling 126 million tons in 1974 the Federal Republic of Germany was the world's third biggest lignite producer, ranking behind East Germany (260 million tons) and the U. S. S. R. (160 million tons). The Rhine Basin accounted for 109 million tons of 1974's total output. The author discusses the lignite reserves of the Rhine Basin, various techniques and equipment used in the opencast mining method by which the lignite in the basin is worked and, finally, focuses on lignite gasification by hydrogenation with the help of nuclear heat.

entry.dc:title: Some of the World's Major Opencast Mining Operations.
entry.dc:creator: de Coussemaker P.
entry.dc:description: The author first presents a brief review of the world's major opencast mining operations, then examines the reasons for which this type of mineral exploitation is elected. Inconveniences and shortcomings of opencast mining are also discussed, along with various techniques and equipment employed, which include drilling, blasting, loading, transport and crushing. The use of computers in large-scale opencast mining is also considered.

entry.dc:title: SNATCHILL EXPERIMENT.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The article reports on an experiment to furnish data on settlement and its effects on houses built on land recently restored after ironstone extraction by opencast mining. The experiment is being conducted on dwellings that have been constructed with conventional foundations on adjoining plots that have been afforded differing ground treatments.

entry.dc:title: Study of the Future Supplies of the Iranian Smelters with Iron Ores.
entry.dc:creator: Bassir S.
entry.prism:publicationName: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: Expansion plans of the Iranian steel industry are briefly outlined. Main problems here involve the selection of smelting method and suitable locations for smelters. The country's rich natural gas deposits would favor a direct reduction of iron ore, which could make a decisive breakthrough with the help of the forthcoming expansion in Iran. The choice of optimal flow of transportation warrants special consideration because the transportation costs play a decisive role in the supply of smelters with iron ore. Exploration activity is reviewed, Iran's major iron ore deposits are presented in tabular form, and opencast mining plans and extraction methods are dealt with.

entry.dc:title: LIGNITE MINING IN GERMANY INVOLVES VAST RECLAMATION/RELOCATION WORK.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The Federal Republic of Germany has considerable coal resources, some of which are recovered by opencast mining methods. Some 62,000-million tons of brown coal in the Republic are largely concentrated (55,000-million tons) in the area of Cologne, Aachen, Duesseldorf. Under present technical and economic conditions, it is estimated that about 35,000-million tons of the deposit can be recovered. Although it is of relatively low thermal value, the brown coal is very suitable for conversion to electrical energy in thermal generating plants.

entry.dc:title: OPENCAST MINING PAVES THE WAY FOR TELFORD NEW TOWN.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The new town of Telford is reaching the third stage of development, having been established by Government decision in 1968. Much of the work to date has included the preparation of land and the provision of services for the projected township of 220,000 people in the 21st century. Telford is unique, not only for the way in which the reclamation of the derelict land has been tackled, but for several large areas scheduled for domestic housing where the derelict land has been reclaimed as a result of opencast coal mining by the NCB. In this way valuable tonnage of steam raising coal for power stations has been won and the pitfallen land with chartered and unchartered shafts has been consolidated thus providing instant building land for houses or the construction of orbital roads.
